robot.name: Dexmate Vega
robot.status_notes: Vega 1 Pro is in production now, sold as a robot platform for developers and researchers. Press reported preorders with a $999 nonrefundable deposit and about three months lead time. No public release date beyond the 2025 preorder was found.
intended_use_cases: product teams building physical AI solutions

height.original_value: Reach floor to 7 ft 2 in (2.2 m); max height (arms raised) 8 ft 2.6 in (2.50 m)
height.notes: Dexmate publishes reach and max height with arms raised, not a standing robot height. Folded height is 26 in (0.66 m). No standing height to top of head was disclosed. The numeric value uses the 2.2 m reach figure.

weight.notes: Official product page value. No conflicting weight found in the other sources.

payload.notes: Official product page says 10+ lbs (5 kg) per arm. Mike Kalil's report says 7 kg (15 lbs) per arm; the official page is used and the conflict is kept in limitations.

runtime.notes: Official product page. Mike Kalil reports the robot's high-capacity battery offers more than 10 hours per charge and up to 30 hours without payload.

battery.notes: Battery capacity was not published in reviewed sources. Dexmate states 20 hours of operation; media reported 10+ hours with payload and up to 30 hours without payload.

degrees_of_freedom.notes: Official page lists Arms 14 (7 each), Torso 3, Head 3, Base 4 (2 steering, 2 drive), total 24. Mike Kalil reported 36 DoF with 3 in head and 13 in arms; the official total is used and the conflict is kept.

walking_speed.notes: No walking speed was published. Vega is wheeled with an omni-directional base, but no speed metric was found.

hands.description: No standard hand is listed. End effectors are ordered separately and include DexGripper S or DexGripper D, user-provided tools, and common third-party end effectors. Research summaries mention Dexmate Vega with Sharpa Wave hands, but this is not a standard configuration.
hands.force_feedback: Optional force/torque (F/T) add-on for admittance control; arms are position-controlled.

items: Stereo RGB camera on a 3-DoF head
Four RGB cameras on the base

compute.description: Official page lists NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor. Mike Kalil reported NVIDIA AGX Orin; the official page is used and the conflict is kept.

actuators.description: Position-controlled arms with optional force/torque add-on; omni-directional base with 2 steering and 2 drive actuators. Actuator type or brand was not disclosed.

availability.notes: The official product page says 'Order now' but does not show a price. Mike Kalil reported $89,999 with a $999 nonrefundable deposit and about three months lead time. End effectors are ordered separately.

manipulation_dexterity.summary: Dexmate discloses two 7-DoF arms with 5 kg payload each, wide end-effector compatibility, and optional force/torque. The official page also summarizes external research claiming dexterous results on Vega, such as DexTacWAM raising success on six contact-rich tasks to 70.6 vs 38.0. No observable demo video content is available from the cited video titles.
caveats: No independent benchmark or success-rate verification is provided.
Demo videos are only titles; no manipulation behavior can be credited from them.
Research summaries are company-published and not the original papers.

autonomy_task_execution.summary: Vega 1 Pro ships as hardware with Python, C++, and Rust APIs and an SDK. Dexmate explicitly says it does not come with AI and the task behavior is yours to build or teach. No autonomous task execution evidence was found.
caveats: The robot is a platform, not an autonomous product.
Teleoperation and data-collection tools are disclosed, but autonomous capabilities are not included.

mobility_whole_body_control.summary: Official page describes an omni-directional base that slides any direction, a 3-DoF torso, 3-DoF head, and 4-DoF base. No speed, fall-recovery, or observed whole-body control demonstration was available.
caveats: No speed metric or mobility test data was published.
Video titles only; no observable mobility behavior.

perception_scene_understanding.summary: Vega includes a stereo RGB head camera, front and rear LiDAR, and four base RGB cameras. No perception algorithm or scene understanding model is included out of the box.
caveats: Sensor hardware is specified, but no perception performance or software stack is provided.

human_interaction.summary: No human interaction capabilities beyond teleoperation interfaces (VR or exoskeleton) were found. Vega is not marketed as an interactive assistant.
caveats: No speech, gesture, or natural interaction claims were found.

endurance_reliability.summary: Dexmate claims 20 hours of operation per charge. Media reported 10+ hours with payload and up to 30 hours without payload. No reliability data, mean time before failure, or long-duration deployment logs were published.
caveats: Runtime is a company spec; no independent test or reliability metric.
Conflicting runtime figures exist between official page and media.

human_environment_fit.summary: Dexmate says the wheeled base cannot fall, the robot can fold to fit through a standard doorway, and it reaches up to 2.2 m. Weight is 135 kg. No full-robot safety certification was found.
caveats: Heavy (135 kg) wheeled platform; no safety certification or indoor/outdoor safety testing disclosed.
Wheeled design is stable but not a biped and may not handle stairs.

deployment_commercial_proof.summary: The robot is purchasable and in production according to Dexmate. The official page names several labs and companies that have published research built on Vega, including UC Berkeley, Stanford, Carnegie Mellon, NVIDIA, Google DeepMind, and Toyota Research Institute. No customer press release or deployment metrics were found.
caveats: Lab research mentions are company-reported; no independent customer deployments or operational metrics.
No named end-customer deployment with hours or output.

accessibility_value.summary: Mike Kalil reports $89,999 with a $999 nonrefundable deposit and about three months lead time. The official product page does not show a price but says 'Order now'.
caveats: Price is from a media blog, not the official page.

researcher_notes.short_verdict_for_arena: Dexmate Vega is a purchasable wheeled humanoid research/developer platform with strong official hardware disclosures (24 DoF, 5 kg per arm, 20 h runtime, sensor suite) but no included autonomy and no observable demo content beyond video titles. Commercial proof is limited to company-reported research-lab adoption and a media-reported $89,999 price.
strongest_positive_evidence: Official product page detailed specs: 2 x 7-DoF arms, 3-DoF torso, 3-DoF head, 4-DoF base, 135 kg, 20-hour runtime, stereoscopic RGB + LiDAR + 4 cameras.
Explicit production and research platform availability.
Company-published research summaries cite quantitative dexterity results on Vega (e.g., DexTacWAM 70.6 vs 38.0).
weakest_or_missing_evidence: No autonomous task execution; no AI included.
No YouTube transcript or observed behavior from video titles.
No walking/mobility speed, battery capacity, hand DoF, or independent benchmark.
No named customer deployments with operational metrics.
conflicting_claims: Payload: official page 5 kg per arm vs Mike Kalil 7 kg per arm.
Runtime: official page 20 hours vs Mike Kalil 10+ hours (up to 30 hours without payload).
DoF: official page 24 total vs Mike Kalil 36 total.
Compute: official page NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor vs Mike Kalil NVIDIA AGX Orin.
do_not_overclaim: Do not call Vega a biped or autononomous humanoid.
Do not credit the YouTube video titles as observed capability demos.
Do not treat Mike Kalil's conflicting specs as canonical over the official Dexmate page.
Do not claim independent customer deployments or industrial pilot metrics.
Do not claim Vega includes AI out of the box.

currentness.currentness_notes: Dexmate Vega 1 Pro is the current purchasable Vega platform as of 2026-10-29. No successor or discontinuation was found in the reviewed sources.

arena_prompt_summary.one_paragraph_summary: Dexmate Vega 1 Pro is a wheeled humanoid research/developer platform from Dexmate in Santa Clara. It has two 7-DoF arms rated at 5 kg each, a 3-DoF torso reaching to 2.2 m, a 3-DoF head, a 4-DoF omni-directional base (24 total DoF), a stereo RGB head camera, front/rear LiDAR, four base RGB cameras, and NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor. Dexmate claims 20 hours of runtime and lists the robot as in production and sold to researchers/developers. A media report prices it at $89,999 with a $999 deposit and cites a lead time of about three months. Vega does not include AI; task behavior is built or taught by the customer using Python/C++/Rust APIs and teleoperation tools. No autonomous task execution or observable demo content was found beyond YouTube video titles. Several research labs are named as having used Vega, but no commercial deployment metrics exist.
strongest_evidence: Official product page detailed hardware specs (payload, DoF, sensors, compute, runtime).
Official statement that Vega 1 Pro is in production and sold as a developer platform.
weakest_evidence: No included autonomy; no autonomous task execution.
No observable demo video content beyond titles.
No walking speed, battery capacity, or hand DoF.
No named customer deployment with metrics.
known_do_not_credit: Do not credit YouTube titles as demonstrated capabilities.
Do not credit Mike Kalil's conflicting specs (7 kg, 36 DoF, AGX Orin, 10+ hour runtime) over the official page.
Do not call Vega a biped or autonomous.
Do not claim industrial/commercial deployments beyond research platform sales.
